themes_detail.label: Industrial Waste Spike
themes_detail.summary: Industrial waste complaints surged to 3 reports 2 weeks ago versus a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2300% spike (z-score: 8.69)—signaling a potential illegal dumping or industrial operation problem in East New York/Cypress Hills that emerged in the past 2 weeks and demands immediate investigation.
evidence: 3 industrial waste complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% increase)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Most severe spike in the dataset by percentage magnitude
reporting_angles: Identify the specific location(s) of industrial waste complaints and interview nearby residents about health impacts
Contact DEP and DSNY to determine if illegal dumping or an unlicensed industrial operation is operating in the district

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Four food poisoning complaints were filed 2 weeks ago against an 8-week average of 0.9 per week—a 357% spike (z-score: 5.21)—suggesting a potential foodborne illness outbreak or problematic food vendor(s) that emerged recently and warrants health department follow-up.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (357% increase)
Z-score of 5.21 indicates statistically significant cluster
Potential public health emergency if complaints are concentrated at single venue or vendor
reporting_angles: Identify which restaurants or food vendors received the complaints and check DOHMH inspection records
Interview affected residents about symptoms, timeline, and suspected food source to determine if outbreak is ongoing

themes_detail.label: House of Worship Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from houses of worship jumped to 6 reports 2 weeks ago from a baseline of 1 per week—a 500% spike (z-score: 4.47)—indicating a sudden escalation in religious institution noise issues that may reflect new activities, equipment, or community tension.
evidence: 6 house of worship noise complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% increase)
Z-score of 4.47 indicates strong statistical significance
Represents the third-largest spike in absolute terms after industrial waste and food poisoning
reporting_angles: Identify which houses of worship are generating complaints and whether they've launched new programs, events, or expanded operations
Interview neighboring residents and the institutions themselves to determine whether this is a temporary event or emerging pattern

themes_detail.label: Water System & Leak Divergence
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints peaked 3 weeks ago at 45 reports (96% above baseline of 23/week, z-score: 4.12), but water leak complaints THIS WEEK dropped 61% to 9 reports—a puzzling divergence suggesting either infrastructure stress with reduced leak reporting or a reporting lag that requires clarification.
evidence: Water system complaints reached 45 (3 weeks ago) vs. 23.0 weekly baseline (96% spike, z-score: 4.12)
Water leak complaints dropped to 9 THIS WEEK vs. 23.0 weekly average (61% decline, z-score: -3.37)
Inverse pattern suggests either major repair work, reporting system change, or unresolved underlying issue
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to determine whether there was a known water main break or repair project 3 weeks ago and whether work is ongoing
Interview residents in affected blocks about whether they experienced water outages, leaks, or pressure issues and whether they received updates

themes_detail.label: Damaged Tree & Homeless Assistance Rise
themes_detail.summary: Damaged tree complaints nearly doubled last week to 11 reports versus a 5.1 weekly average (115% spike, z-score: 3.09), while homeless person assistance requests rose 107% to 7 complaints 3 weeks ago—two separate infrastructure and social support signals appearing within a month that may reflect storm damage and growing street homelessness.
evidence: 11 damaged tree complaints filed last week vs. 5.1 weekly average (115% increase, z-score: 3.09)
7 homeless person assistance complaints filed 3 weeks ago vs. 3.4 weekly average (107% increase, z-score: 2.98)
Aligns with community board's repeated requests for homeless shelter expansion and park/amenity improvements
reporting_angles: Determine whether recent severe weather caused the tree damage spike and assess Parks Department response timeline
Investigate the nature of homeless assistance complaints and cross-reference with DHS outreach activity to identify unmet needs in sheltering and services
